newsitem.title: UK: Britain must keep EMU options open - Heseltine.
newsitem.headline: Britain must keep EMU options open - Heseltine.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine said on Wednesday that Britain must keep its options open on a single currency and make its mind up whether to join, when the time comes, based on facts not theory.

Heseltine told BBC radio that it would be an abdication of Britain's self-interest if it was not represented at negotiations on a single currency because it had closed off the option of participation.

He said it might be in Britain's interest to join EMU in the first wave because the interests of its important banking and finance sectors would be inextricably interwoven with the single currency. If the conditions were right, a single currency would also provide stability that would attract exporters.
But he said there were also counter-arguments, which meant the government had to keep its options open.
"There are arguments both ways. The judgement must be based not upon theories of what may or may not be the case, but upon the facts of what are the case when you make the judgement," Heseltine said.
He said the failure of members of the the ruling Conservative party to stick to the government's established line could only harm the party's chances of re-election.

"What they're doing is creating an impression of disunity,the only consequence of which can be to put into power a Labour government infinitely worse in terms of selling out British interests," Heseltine said.
Heseltine was speaking soon after former Conservative leadership challenger John Redwood again urged the government to rule out membership of a single currency.
"It would be an abdication of our self-interest if we were not at that negotiating forum...seeking to enhance, protect, defend Britain's vital interest in this critical field," Heseltine replied.
